objectives.description: New shared library batch-gate-marker-lib.sh (path, staleness window, fail-open helpers)
orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh writes the marker; drops the -gt 1 directive gate
orchestrate-batch-gate.sh removes the marker at discharge, idempotently
Test coverage split across three homes; batch-gate-marker-lib.sh declared

approaches_tried.approach: A dedicated, from-scratch fixture suite for the marker write/removal behavior
approaches_tried.reason: orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's own existing test fixture is 6600+ lines; standing up an equivalent fixture from scratch for 2 new assertions would be enormously more costly than reusing an existing live (non-dry-run) implement-dispatch case already present in its Group 4/5. Reused instead; the dedicated new suite (test-batch-gate-pending-marker.sh) owns only the library's pure functions.

notes: Adding batch-gate-marker-lib.sh as a new orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh dependency broke every case in test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh and test-orchestrate-batch-gate.sh downstream of the first sandbox setup, because their fixture sandboxes copy a curated, hand-maintained list of lib/*.sh files and had no entry for a lib that did not exist yet at suite-authoring time. Fixed by adding the new lib to both suites' copy lists (444 passed/0 failed; 29 passed/0 failed respectively). A third, independently-maintained fixture (test-force-phases.sh) had the exact same gap; fixed identically (36 passed/0 failed). A verify-touched.sh run against the still-undeployed tree continues to report test-force-phases.sh as a NEW failure after this fix -- confirmed as pre-deploy staleness (deployed copy has zero references to the new lib; source-store copy has four), not a regression, resolving at Phase 8's redeploy.
